data.name: Ibha
data.gender_notes: Ibha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ibha is a Sanskrit name derived from the root word 'ibh', which means 'to desire'. The name signifies one's innermost wish or intention. In Hindu mythology, Ibha is the name of a goddess who is believed to fulfill the desires of her devotees. The name Ibha carries the meaning “Desire, Wish, Intention” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ibha usually hope their child will grow to embody desire, wish, intention and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Manifestation of inner desires and intentions
data.etymology: Ibha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Desire, Wish, Intention.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ibha total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ibha has a rich cultural significance in Hinduism, as it is the name of a goddess sometimes referred to as 'Greater Lakshmi' or 'Lakshmi Sakti'. Hindus believes that Ibha, also known as 'Manikam', is the presiding deity of wealth and prosperity. She is regarded as the embodiment of the ever-desiring soul, and is worshipped to fulfill material and spiritual desires. The name is particularly popular in certain regions, such as Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh in India.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ibha holds deep spiritual significance, as it symbolizes the inner longing and desire for perfection and enlightenment. It reminds us of our ultimate goal as beings - to transcend our desires and connect with the divine. By invoking the name Ibha, one can call upon the goddess to purify the mind of attachments and help one focus on the essential aspects of life, ultimately leading to spiritual growth and self-realization.
